The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click ResellerProfitTracker.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on adding items, recording sales, true profit and backups.
  4. Follow the three steps on Home: add your inventory, say where it’s listed, and record a sale when one sells.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on Home or in Settings & backup. Thrift & Thread, a fictional reseller with 14 months of sales on five platforms, a lot, a bundle and two returns, fills every screen, and nothing in it is saved. Return to my shop brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

True profit, after every cost.

Home shows this month’s profit after what the items cost you, the platform fees, the shipping labels and your running costs.

WordWhat it means
True profitPrice and shipping charged, minus fees, the label, other costs and what the item cost you.
ROIProfit ÷ what the item cost you. 300% means it made three times its cost.
Cost of goods soldWhat the items you sold (or wrote off) cost you.
Running costsSupplies, storage, apps and subscriptions: costs that belong to no one item.

After a haul

Add a whole haul in a minute.

Add inventory: set the date and where you bought once, then type a title and what you paid and press Enter. The next row is ready straight away.

Bought a lot

A bin, a bundle or a storage unit for one price? Use Bought a lot: its price is split evenly across the items you add, or by their list prices. The shares always add up to the cent.

Several of the same

Set the quantity, like 12 of the same card lot. A sale can sell one or several; each one sold costs its share.

Your inventory

Every item, and what it should make.

Inventory shows each item’s cost, list price, where it’s listed and the estimated profit after typical fees. Add a photo, brand and size in its Edit.

FiltersOn the shelf, Not listed, Listed, Over 90 days, Sold, Gone. Grid, Compact or Table; search by title, SKU or brand.
Over 90 daysStock that isn’t moving. A price drop, a new photo or another platform can help; Home reminds you.
Donated, lost or keptEdit the item and pick what happened. Donated and lost are written off; kept for yourself isn’t a business cost.

When it sells

Record the sale, see the profit.

Click Sold on the item (or Record a sale). Pick the platform and the price: the usual fee is filled in for you to check, and the profit shows before you save.

Returns

On the sale, choose Return: how much you refunded, whether the item came back (it goes back on the shelf) and any fee the platform gave back.

Platform fees

Fees change. Check the starting fees under Platforms and edit them with Save fees. Past sales keep the fee they paid.

Reseller Profit Tracker | JPS Digital Pages6
R
Tax time

Schedule C, cost of goods included.

Schedule C lays out your year: gross receipts, returns, cost of goods sold from your inventory, and every expense on its line. Print it or Export CSV.

Running costs and mileage

Add an expense once; monthly ones repeat. Log a trip for sourcing runs and the post office; set the mileage rate under Settings → Your shop.

Profit & loss

Any dates, for the whole shop or one platform. Bank or card CSV? Import bank CSV brings in running costs; you check each line.

A worksheet, not tax advice. Ask a tax pro about your own situation.

Keeping your shop safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every item, lot, sale, return, expense, trip and platform fee. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
A profit looks too highThe item may have no cost. Edit it and add what you paid; Home lists items with no cost.
A fee looks wrongOpen the sale and type the fee the platform actually kept. Then update that platform under Platforms.
A returned item vanishedOpen the sale → Return and tick “The item came back”. It goes back on the shelf.
My bank import has personal spendingSet those lines to Skip before importing. Only business costs belong here.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
